title: Client DPA execution & signing playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is an operational checklist and script for Sales/CS/Legal to use when executing Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with clients. It consolidates common negotiation positions, an approval flow, execution templates, and the evidence package we attach to completed DPAs for audit and customer assurance.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to standard hosted API and Dedicated customers.
- Private/on-prem customers may require additional annexes; see Private DPA annex checklist.
- This is not a replacement for legal advice on unusual clauses; escalate per escalation matrix.

Quick reference (one-line):
- Sales/CS: follow pre-sign checklist, use signing script, collect signatures, upload executed DPA and evidence to Contracts repo and Confluence page.
- Security/Legal: review redlines as-needed within 48 hours, approve or resolve escalations within 5 business days.

Pre-sign checklist (Sales / Solutions engineer):
1) Confirm customer type and required DPA variant (hosted | dedicated | private).
2) Identify any regulatory constraints (e.g., GDPR, UK GDPR, HIPAA, PDPA) and flag to Legal.
3) Verify data flows with Solutions: where customer data will be processed (region/region fallbacks), whether customer uploads model weights, and whether any sensitive categories are in scope.
4) Confirm encryption/KMS requirements and whether customer will supply keys.
5) Check existing master services agreement (MSA) terms for references to DPA; note signature authority on both sides.
6) Create a Contract ticket (JIRA-xxxx) and attach the draft DPA.
7) If customer proposes material changes, ask for a consolidated redline (one file) and mark the negotiation deadline.

Common negotiation positions (playbook stance):
- Data scope: Accept narrow "processing of customer content and metadata" language. Resist broad "any data" formulations.
- Subprocessors: Accept Redwood standard subprocessor clause with 30-day notice. For large enterprise requests for pre-approval, escalate to Legal and Customer Success.
- Data residency: Offer region-limited processing where technically available; use data residency exhibit.
- Liability cap: Maintain standard cap in MSA; do not move to unlimited liability for data incidents. Escalate if customer insists.
- Deletion and return: Accept short retention periods; ensure we can meet deletion obligations operationally before agreeing.
- Audit rights: Offer supplier-attestation package and SOC/GRC artifacts; deny continuous on-site audits absent escalated enterprise need.
- Encryption/KMS: If customer requires BYOK/HSM, route to Private/Enterprise sales and EngOps.

Redline handling process (Legal / Security):
1) Triage redline within 24 business hours. Classify as: non-material (accept), operational (requires Eng/SRE signoff), legal/risk (requires Legal review), or blocker (escalate).
2) For operational items, create a short tech FAQ and route to EngOps/Infra for feasibility (+48 hours).
3) Legal drafts counterproposal language and returns single consolidated redline.
4) Record all versions in the Contracts GitHub repo and the JIRA ticket.

Execution and signature flow (recommended):
- Preferred: e-sign via DocuSign (template ID: DOCU-DPA-V2). Sales initiates envelope to customer signer and internal signer (Head of Revenue or delegated signatory).
- Fallback: PDF executed via email with signature block and signature page scanned.
- When to require wet signature: only for high-risk/regulatory customers or when requested by customer procurement.

Signature script (CS / Sales template):
Email subject: "Redwood DPA for signature — [Customer]"
Email body (short):
"Hi [Name],
Attached is the DPA aligned to our MSA and the data processing scope we discussed. This version reflects the [hosted/dedicated/private] profile. If you’re comfortable, please sign via the DocuSign link. If you need a single consolidated redline back, please return it by [date].
Thanks — [Your name], Redwood Customer Success"

Evidence package to attach after execution (what to store/upload):
- Fully executed PDF of DPA (file name convention: company-dpa-YYYYMMDD.pdf)
- Signed signature page (if separate)
- Redline history (if any) and final consolidated comments log
- Contract JIRA ticket id and brief summary of concessions
- Mapping of data flows (screenshot or Confluence link) showing processing regions
- KMS/Encryption notes (if BYOK/HSM involved) or link to customer key policy
- Copy of any additional exhibits (SLA, on-prem annex)
- Audit evidence package pointer: SOC2 report link and date, penetration test summary date
- Ownership and retention metadata (who uploaded, date uploaded, storage location)

Storage and audit steps (post-sign):
1) Upload artifact set to Contracts GitHub (private) and Confluence contract record.
2) Tag the DPA page with customer name and JIRA ticket.
3) Notify Security/GRC mailbox with proof-of-execution and path.
4) If customer requested evidence (e.g., SOC2), confirm access/links are still valid and share per agreed mechanism.

Escalation matrix and SLAs for review: 
- First-level triage: Security Operations (1 business day)
- Legal review: 2–5 business days depending on complexity
- Executive escalation: VP Security or General Counsel if liability/indemnity or cross-border data transfer exceptions are requested

Playbook examples (practical quick answers):
- Customer asks for continuous on-site audits: Offer scheduled evidence package + limited remote access to logs; escalate to Legal for exceptions.
- Customer pushes for unlimited liability for GDPR fines: Reject; propose reasonable indemnity limited to proven direct damages and regulatory fines carve-outs per MSA.
- Customer requests deletion within 24 hours of ingestion: Check ops feasibility; for streaming use-cases we will accept reasonable deletion timelines (48–72 hours) or propose a data-retention exhibit.

Templates and snippets (for Legal/Sales to copy):
- Acceptable subprocessor acceptance sentence: "Processor will maintain a list of sub-processors and provide 30 days' prior notice of material changes with an opportunity to object."
- Default data residency exhibit header: "Customer Data will be stored and processed within the geographic region(s) identified in Schedule A, except for transient processing in other regions for failover or caching."
- Minimal audit response: "Processor will provide access to attestations and third-party audit reports upon execution of a standard NDA and as subject to request frequency limits in this agreement."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define threshold for when we move a customer from Hosted to Dedicated purely for contractual residency guarantees (owner: Product Ops).
- Standardize the docu sign template metadata so the Contracts repo can be programmatically updated on signature (owner: Eng Tools).
- Build a one-click evidence bundle generator in Confluence that assembles documents from known locations (owner: Security Automation).

Retention and review cadence:
- Store executed DPAs perpetually in Contracts repo with metadata. Security should review high-risk DPAs quarterly.
- Legal to produce an annual summary of significant DPA concessions for executive review.

Appendix: quick links and assets
- DPA templates page: confluence://security/dpa-templates
- Contracts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts 
- DocuSign template id: DOCU-DPA-V2
- Evidence upload instructions: confluence://security/evidence-upload-guide

Notes to self / working items (informal):
- Consider adding a short customer-facing one-pager that explains SOC2/Security artifacts we can provide during procurement.
- We get repeated requests for data access logs — decide which customers get on-demand log snapshots vs periodic reports.

Contact points:
- Security contact: security-ops@redwood.com (Rosa Martinez)
- Legal contact: contracts@redwood.com (Aisha Patel)
- Escalation: vp-security@redwood.com

End of playbook.

Document history: draft created by Marcus Nguyen 2024-11-15; updated with Legal feedback 2025-02-10.
